niche: a subscription language-tutoring platform deciding whether to re-run its autumn 2026 acquisition campaign at the same cost per paid member, judged on the cost of each campaign member still paying in their twelfth month, when the campaign's members were matched en masse to tutors onboarded in the autumn after a six-month onboarding pause
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans the billing ledger (retries, refunds, replayed rows), applies the growth review standard's definitions, builds the members' paid-retention curve by membership month from every 2024 to 2026 membership, checks it against the spring 2025 campaign and projects each autumn member to the twelfth charge files about EUR 560 per twelfth-month member and books the re-run; the call is wrong because the autumn members sit with tutors in their first teaching months, tutors stop teaching at their highest rates between their fourth and eighth months, and a member whose tutor stops cancels about half the time, so the expected twelfth-month members are about a sixth fewer and the cost is about EUR 670.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a campaign cohort's expected twelfth-month paid retention, projected from immature membership histories, the retention and lifetime-value task type's own estimate; what decides it is how a two-sided tutoring marketplace's supply churn carries into member churn through each member's tutor, so with another field's nouns the monthly billing clock, the campaign payback rule and the surge matching of new members to new tutors stop making sense.
layer1: card charges retried up to three times inside a dunning window, the successful retry being the month's charge
first charges refunded in full inside the fourteen-day cooling-off period
webhook replays writing the same charge twice
an amount column renamed and moved to minor units in the 2025 billing export
plan codes renamed at the April 2025 price change
tutor ids written with and without their T- prefix across two lesson-log exports
campaign codes in several cases and with channel suffixes in the attribution export
agency invoices in EUR and GBP, net and VAT lines, one credit note
stakeholder_role: the head of growth, who books or cancels the agency's spring flight

world.geography: Germany (Berlin) with members in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands and the UK
world.org_type: a subscription platform matching each member with a dedicated freelance language tutor

driver: A unit's chance of reaching a milestone is set largely by whether the provider it is attached to keeps operating, providers stop at a rate that peaks a few months into their own tenure, and the forward group was attached almost wholly to providers in their first months, so an exit curve by the unit's own tenure, which validates on closed groups, overstates how many reach the milestone.
driver_concrete: Each autumn 2026 campaign member's chance of paying a twelfth monthly charge is projected through their tutor: tutors stop teaching at about 13 to 18 per cent a month in their fourth to eighth teaching months against about 1 per cent after a year, a member whose tutor stops cancels about half the time within two charges, and 4 in 5 autumn members were matched to tutors who began teaching in September to November 2026, so the expected twelfth-month members fall about a sixth below the membership-month curve and the cost per twelfth-month member rises from about EUR 560 to about EUR 670.
stump: A competent solver projects the autumn campaign's members on the platform's paid-retention curve by membership month, validated on the spring 2025 campaign, and files about EUR 560 per twelfth-month member, inside the EUR 610 bar, and books the re-run; the step that lands it there is projecting each member on their own tenure when the member's cancellation rides on their tutor, and the autumn members' tutors are about to cross the months in which new tutors stop teaching.
deep_chain: (1) rebuild each member's current tutor and each tutor's teaching months from the lesson log, which holds no tenure; (2) measure from every past tutor stop that a member whose tutor stops teaching cancels about half the time within two charges, net of their own baseline; (3) estimate tutors' stopping by teaching month from every tutor's history, a hump in months four to eight; (4) recognise that the autumn members sit with tutors in their first three teaching months, unlike any earlier group bar part of the spring 2025 campaign; (5) project each member to the twelfth charge through their tutor's stopping odds and their own cancellation curve estimated on months with an active tutor, so stops are not counted twice; (6) check the linked projection out of sample against the membership-month curve; (7) cost per twelfth-month member against EUR 610.
judgment: That a member's retention is a function of their tutor's survival rather than of their own tenure alone, carried as a two-level projection; the data justify it through the cancellation spike after every tutor stop, the tutor stopping hump by teaching month, and the membership-month curve's miscalibration for members of young tutors on held-out 2026 months.
one_fact_test: The likeliest hint is that members often leave when their tutor stops teaching; told that, a run still has to see that stopping depends on the tutor's teaching month and that the autumn tutors are new (the pooled tutor stop rate files about EUR 575 and the re-run), estimate the members' own curve on active-tutor months so stops are not counted twice, and carry each member through the projection.
strategy_label: WORKS IN FORM: heterogeneity decides through weighting to the forward group (the autumn members' tutor teaching months), the property rebuilt from the lesson log, never read off a column; outcomes not finished (the tutors' stops still to come)

differentiation.task156: task156 scales how often a fixed capacity is exceeded by the share of a network below a fluctuating level read from a second record; here nothing is exceeded and no level fluctuates: each member's chance of a twelfth charge runs through whether their tutor keeps teaching, a two-level survival carried member by member through the tutors' own stopping curve.
differentiation.task134: task134 prices each lot's rebuild chance against a payoff threshold and a cost step; here no payoff is computed: the yield is a member's survival conditioned on the survival of the tutor they were matched to, and the forward group's tutors sit at the start of their stopping hump.
differentiation.task165: task165 conditions an upgrade's gain on how much the old service level already treated, read from each unit's own record; here nothing is upgraded: the forward members were matched almost wholly to tutors in their first teaching months, and each member is projected through that tutor's chance of stopping.
differentiation.task173: task173 adds work-induced failure chances from a visit schedule (its first architecture conditioned comebacks on the opener's desk tenure); here the provider's tenure matters because the provider itself stops on a hump and takes about half its members with it, so the projection runs through the provider's survival rather than a rate conditioned on who served.
